selected_result: Langlois–Louvet Theorem 7 and equation (16): a condition-number criterion guaranteeing faithful rounding by compensated Horner

bibliographic_source.title: Faithful Polynomial Evaluation with Compensated Horner Algorithm

paper_locations.anchor: Floating-point predecessor and successor, faithful rounding, round-to-nearest arithmetic, global no-overflow/no-underflow assumption
Exact residual polynomials and compensated Horner result

task_clarification: For a degree n polynomial p with floating coefficients and a floating argument x, use the exact Algorithm 6 CompHorner result, with Algorithm 5 EFTHorner inside it.

Define cond(p,x)=tilde_p(x)/|p(x)| on the nonzero-evaluation domain. Under the strict equation (16) criterion cond(p,x) < ((1-u)/(2+u))*u/gamma_(2n)^2, the computed result is a faithful rounding of the exact p(x) in the paper's predecessor/successor sense.
Retain the source's round-to-nearest, no-overflow, and no-underflow assumptions and the mathematical meaning of the floating-point neighbour relation.
scope_constraints: Do not replace CompHorner by ordinary Horner or by an unspecified algorithm satisfying a preassumed accuracy contract.
Do not replace faithful rounding with a relative-error or sign-only conclusion; preserve the predecessor/successor semantics.
Preserve the strict inequality and exact coefficient (1-u)/(2+u), including the gamma_(2n)^2 denominator.
The source's condition number requires p(x)≠0; include this as a well-definedness guard rather than silently defining a misleading value at zero.
The source's Theorem 7 statement does not repeat its global no-underflow/no-overflow assumptions; they still apply.
